original_question: Can one construct smooth-atlas globalisations of the known Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetries Q_{1:6/2}(P)=O→r(γ_3)(P), Q_5(P)=O→r(γ_5)(P), and Q_7(P)=O→r(γ_7)(P)? In this notation, O→r is the graph-orientation map that sends a graph cocycle γ to a universal infinitesimal symmetry Q(P) of Poisson bi-vectors.
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the paper’s cohomological/differential-geometric open problem about whether the known Kontsevich graph flows on affine Poisson manifolds can be understood globally through the smooth structure of the manifold, rather than only through the affine-chart construction required by the orientation morphism. In the paper’s overview, this is the class of problems concerning the Poisson-(non)triviality of the universal flows and the action of the known symmetries on "nearly generic" Poisson brackets. ([indico.math.cnrs.fr](https://indico.math.cnrs.fr/event/5243/attachments/2501/3099/CAP19_TitresAbstracts.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the specific known cocycles γ_3, γ_5, and γ_7 and the corresponding oriented universal infinitesimal symmetries Q_{1:6/2}, Q_5, and Q_7 produced by the graph-orientation morphism. It also correctly targets the paper’s differential-geometric/globalisation direction, not the separate combinatorial questions about graph cocycles or Leibniz-graph factorizations. ([research.rug.nl](https://research.rug.nl/en/publications/the-orientation-morphism-from-graph-cocycles-to-deformations-of-p?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The ambient geometric setting should be stated explicitly: real finite-dimensional affine manifolds M^r equipped with Poisson bi-vectors P; the orientation morphism is universal with respect to affine Poisson manifolds, not arbitrary smooth manifolds from the outset.

The paper-critical distinction between an affine atlas and a smooth atlas is missing. Kontsevich’s graph construction uses affine-coordinate changes x' = Ax + b, whereas the sought globalisation concerns interpretation via the manifold’s smooth structure and diffeomorphisms.

The question should specify what 'globalisation' means in this context: namely, realizing the infinitesimal cocycle Q(P) as a Poisson coboundary Q(P) = [[X, P]] for a globally defined vector field X, whose flow gives (generally nonlinear) diffeomorphisms.

The draft does not say that the issue is tied to Poisson cohomology exactness/triviality of the graph flow, which is the paper’s cohomological formulation of the same differential-geometric direction.

The quantifier should be clarified: is the question being asked for each of the known cocycles γ_3, γ_5, γ_7, for all Poisson bi-vectors P in the intended class, or only for some Poisson manifolds/classes of examples?
The draft should indicate that these are the currently known proper nonlinear universal graph symmetries discussed by the author (tetrahedral, pentagon-wheel, heptagon-wheel cases).

The phrase 'smooth-atlas globalisations' is too compressed unless one also says that the intended outcome is an interpretation of the graph flows as infinitesimal diffeomorphism actions coming from the smooth structure, rather than merely affine-chart formulas.

The notation O→r should be explained as the orientation morphism from graph cocycles to universal infinitesimal symmetries of Poisson bi-vectors on affine manifolds; as written, the draft assumes this without reintroducing the affine-manifold restriction.
refined_question: Let (M^r, P) be a real finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifold, and let Q_{1:6/2}(P) = O→r(γ_3)(P), Q_5(P) = O→r(γ_5)(P), and Q_7(P) = O→r(γ_7)(P) be the known universal Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetries (tetrahedral, pentagon-wheel, and heptagon-wheel). Can these affine-atlas-defined graph flows be globalized to the smooth structure of M by finding globally defined vector fields X_{γ,P} such that Q(P) = [[X_{γ,P}, P]], so that the known graph symmetries arise as infinitesimal diffeomorphism actions in a smooth atlas rather than only through the affine-coordinate construction of the orientation morphism?
justification: The author’s CAP19 abstract for this paper separates four classes of open problems and explicitly includes both the cohomological question of whether the universal flows are nontrivial in Poisson cohomology and the differential-geometric/PDE questions coming from the action of the known symmetries on nearly generic Poisson brackets. That is the closest official formulation to your draft. A later paper by the same author, explicitly citing [10] = arXiv:1910.05844, unpacks this direction in the precise form relevant to your wording: Kontsevich’s construction itself needs an affine structure, while a 'smooth-atlas' reading amounts to asking whether a graph flow Q(P) is exact, Q(P) = [[X, P]], for a globally defined vector field X whose flow gives nonlinear diffeomorphisms, potentially allowing the stock of graph flows to imitate smooth structure. So your draft is substantively on target, but it needs the affine-versus-smooth distinction and the Poisson-cohomology/coboundary formulation to be paper-faithful and stand-alone. ([indico.math.cnrs.fr](https://indico.math.cnrs.fr/event/5243/attachments/2501/3099/CAP19_TitresAbstracts.pdf))
